title: Tried generating some playable 3D mini-games with Hy4 preview. Better at layout than expected.
author: jade_jade_jade_jade
selftext:
I have been testing different prompt-to-game setups lately. Ran a few tests on the new Hy4 preview setup with their workbench tool, and the 3D rendering side is worth talking about.

Usually, when you ask an LLM to build interactive scenes purely from text, the physics break immediately or the visual depth looks completely flat. In these runs, the model actually handled lighting, asset placement, and basic camera controls without needing manual fixes right away. tested a few simple ideas like top-down runners and basic mini-games. You type the idea into the workbench and it gives you a live preview you can play with right away. 

It is not going to replace a full game engine workflow anytime soon. Still, for rapid grayboxing, testing visual themes, or putting together a quick vertical slice idea in five minutes, it feels way more practical than older generative tools.

Anyone here actually using generative tools during the blockout/prototyping stage, or do you still prefer doing the whole early phase manually?
